title: SpaceX lenders don’t want Elon Musk launching their collateral into space
author: Michelle Chan, Financial Times
summary_long: Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his plan for orbital data centers. The world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips. id: bigtech:maha pac spent more on steak luxury club than candidates rep:2026-11-19T21:19:12.000Z
title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
author: Beth Mole
summary_long: In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement's midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA's own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group's priority was ever winning elections in the first place. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA's clout in the midterms. Source: arstechnica.com. id: ai_data:active feature acquisition by distilling an oracle teacher:2026-11-19T18:52:57.000Z
title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
author: Yang Meng
summary_long: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. Source: arxiv.org. id: ai_data:geohunter mapping a generative engine optimization network i:2026-11-19T18:33:42.000Z
title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
author: Sean Tang
summary_long: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. id: ai_data:one framework to diagnose them all a stratified benchmark fo:2026-11-19T16:15:38.000Z
title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
author: Asif Shahriyar Sushmit
summary_long: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale. Alikbachan is a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified along three crossed axes: a human-validated cultural-distance band, six task types, and a five-family, 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. It comprises a harvested 2,516-item test set (Phase 1) and a quota-constructed, gold-labeled 5,000-item set (Phase 2). Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-11-19.
